SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_ge¶

Back to SeriesTraverseAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_ge(double rhs) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_ge(const Series& rhs) const;

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_ge(double rhs) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_ge(const Series& rhs) const;

The mirror method find_le has the same shape and returns positions at or below the threshold.

What It Does¶

find_ge(rhs) returns the coordinates of every position whose value is greater than or equal to rhs. It is find_all with the mask source.ge(rhs) built for you.

  • find_ge(double) uses one scalar threshold for the whole Series.

  • find_ge(const Series&) uses a broadcast peer, so the threshold can vary by row, column, or position — useful for “which values exceed this row’s own mean,” and similar per-lane tests.

The comparison is inclusive (>=). For a strict > build the mask yourself and call find_all, or use find_btw with the exclusive flag.

Parameters¶

rhs (double or const Series&)

The lower bound. A Series rhs broadcasts against the traversed shape.

Returns¶

TraverseMatch Row-major coordinates and matched values of the positions at or above the bound. K can be 0.

Gradient¶

Coordinates carry no gradient. match.values() and match.select_from(other) are differentiable gathers.

Examples¶

Example 1. A scalar threshold, and the several views the result offers.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto hits = grid.traverse.find_ge(6.0);

std::cout << "count=" << hits.count() << "\n";
std::cout << "coords=" << hits.coords();
std::cout << "values=" << hits.values();
std::cout << "linear=" << hits.linear_indices();

Output¶

count=5
coords=pluss::Series(shape=[5,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=10, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 0],
  [0, 2],
  [1, 1],
  [1, 2],
  [2, 0]]
values=pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[10, 7, 9, 6, 8]
linear=pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 2, 4, 5, 6]

linear_indices() are the flat row-major offsets: grid[0,0] is offset 0, grid[1,2] is offset 5.

Example 2. A per-column threshold with a Series right-hand side.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto floor = pluss::make_series({5.0, 5.0, 5.0});
std::cout << "count=" << grid.traverse.find_ge(floor).count();

Output¶

count=6

Example 3. Restrict the search to one row with the proxy form.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto row1 = grid.traverse({std::int64_t{1}}).find_ge(5.0);

std::cout << "count=" << row1.count() << "  rank=" << row1.rank() << "\n";
std::cout << row1.coords();
std::cout << row1.values();

Output¶

count=2  rank=1
pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[1],
  [2]]
pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[9, 6]

The sub-view is one-dimensional, so rank() is 1 and the coordinates index the three columns of row 1 — position 1 (9) and position 2 (6).

Example 4. values() participates in a training graph.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});
grid.tracks_slope_(true);

grid.traverse.find_ge(6.0).values().sum().reverse();

std::cout << grid.sensitivity();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 1],
  [0, 1, 1],
  [1, 0, 0]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The bound is inclusive. Use find_all with source.gt(rhs) for a strict comparison.

  • With traverse({ on }), coordinates are relative to the sub-view and rank() is the sub-view’s rank.

  • A Series rhs must broadcast to the traversed shape.

  • Coordinates and offsets are non-differentiable; values() and select_from() are.

Summary¶

find_ge(rhs) finds every position at or above a scalar or broadcast bound:

  • convenience over find_all with a ge mask

  • find_le is the at-or-below mirror

  • inclusive comparison; empty match when nothing qualifies

See Also¶

  • find_le: the at-or-below mirror.

  • find_btw: a two-sided band, inclusive or exclusive.

  • find_all: supply a strict > mask yourself.

  • TraverseMatch: the result object.
